questions.question: Which river basin originates from the Western Ghats range of Karnataka state and has many tributaries such as the Noyyal, Kabini, Arkavathi and Amaravati?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kaveri.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The river basin that originates from the** Western Ghats** range of **Karnataka state** is the Kaveri River Basin.
 
• The Kaveri River Basin is one of the major river basins in India and covers parts of **Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala.**
 
• The** Noyyal, Kabini, Arkavathi, and Amaravati** are some of the important tributaries of the Kaveri River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sabarmati** flows westward in India.

 
 
• **It starts in the Aravalli Range in the Udaipur District of Rajasthan and travels 371 km in a south-westerly direction throughout Rajasthan and Gujarat before meeting the Gulf of Khambhat of the Arabian Sea.**
 
 
 
• In eastern India's state of **Odisha**, there is a significant seasonal river called the **Brahmani**.
 
 
• **The Brahmani river travels through the districts of Sundargarh, Deogarh, Angul, Dhenkanal, Cuttack, Jajapur, and Kendrapara.**
 
• It is produced by the confluence of the Sankh and South Koel rivers.
 
 
 
• Periyar is a longest river in Kerala having large discharge potential.
 
 
• **It is one of the few rivers that flows year-round in the area and supplies drinking water to a number of sizable communities.**

questions.question: Which s-block element is a silvery- metal that is used in an alloy with copper or nickel to make gyroscopes, springs, electrical contacts, spot-welding electrodes, and non-sparking equipment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beryllium**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The s-block element that is a silvery- metal and is used in an alloy with copper or nickel to make various equipment is Beryllium.**
 
• Beryllium is a lightweight and strong metal that is widely used in aerospace, defense, and nuclear industries.
 
• **It has a high melting point, good thermal conductivity, and is also a good electrical conductor.**
 
• **Atomic **number of Beryllium is - **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rubidium is a soft, silvery- metal that is highly reactive.**

 
 
• **It is used in atomic clocks and as a catalyst in certain chemical reactions.**
 
 
 
• Francium is a highly radioactive and unstable element.
 
 
• **It is extremely rare and has no practical applications.**
 
 
 
• Caesium is a soft, silvery-golden metal that is also highly reactive.
 
 
• **It is used in atomic clocks, drilling fluids, and in the treatment of cancer.**

questions.question: Which gas is the major component of biogas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Biogas is primarily composed of **methane gas**, which is the major component of biogas.
 
• **Methane gas makes up about 50-75% of biogas, while the remaining 25-50% is made up of carbon dioxide, water vapor, and trace amounts of other gases.**
 
• Biogas is a gaseous** renewable **energy source.
 
• Anaerobic digestion using methanogens or anaerobic organisms in a bioreactor, biodigester, or anaerobic digester produces biogas.
 
• **The main components of the gas are methane (CH₄) and carbon dioxide (CO₂), with trace amounts of moisture, siloxanes, and hydrogen sulfide (H₂S). **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Compressed natural gas:**

 
 
• CNG is a** fossil fuel** that is primarily composed of **methane gas**.
 
• **CNG is commonly used as a fuel for vehicles and is produced from natural gas reserves.**
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen gas:**
 
 
• **It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless, and highly flammable gas.**
 
• It is commonly used in fuel cells to generate electricity.
 
 
 
• **Liquefied petroleum gas:**
 
 
• It is a mixture of **propane** and** butane** gases.
 
• **It is commonly used as a fuel for heating and cooking.**

questions.question: What is the total route length of the Indian Railways (as of March 2020)?

__
 
• **Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world and connects almost all parts of India through its extensive network of tracks.**
 
• **As of March 2020, the total route length of the Indian Railways is 67,956 km, which includes both broad gauge and meter gauge tracks.**
 
• The Indian Railways has 18 zones and more than 7,000 stations, making it an integral part of the country's transportation infrastructure.
 
• The Indian Railways also operates several luxury and tourist trains, such as the Palace on Wheels and the Maharaja Express, which offer a unique and memorable travel experience to passengers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In an effort to boost tourism in Rajasthan, the Indian Railways and the Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation jointly launched it.
 
• In 1982, the train was introduced.
 
• Heritage Palace on Wheels is the new name for the train.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation is the owner and operator of the opulent tourist train known as the Maharajas' Express.**
 
 
• Between October and April, it operates four routes through North-West and Central India, with a primary focus on Rajasthan.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam is a dance form of which state?

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of **Kerala**, India.
 
• Mohiniyattam is primarily a** **solo dance performed by women and is known for its graceful movements and expressions.
 
• The dance form originated in the temples of Kerala and was performed by **devadasis** (temple dancers) to entertain the deities.
 
• **The word Mohiniyattam is derived from two words, "Mohini" (meaning enchantress) and "attam" (meaning dance). The dance form is said to have been named after Mohini, the female avatar of Lord Vishnu.**
 
• **Mohiniyattam is characterized by subtle movements, intricate footwork, and expressive facial expressions.**
 
• **The costumes worn by the dancers are usually white or off-white with gold borders and are adorned with jewelry and flowers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Tamil Nadu is known for its classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam.**
 
• **Maharashtra is known for its folk dances like Lavani, Koli, and Tamasha.**

questions.question: Based on the recommendations of which Committee was the creation of a separate category for NBFCS operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malegam Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The creation of a separate category for NBFCs operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) was done based on the recommendations of the Malegam Committee.**
 
• The Malegam Committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2010 to review the microfinance sector in India and provide recommendations for its growth and development.
 
• The committee recommended the creation of a separate category of NBFCs for microfinance to regulate and supervise them effectively, and to ensure that they comply with the prescribed norms and standards.
 
• The NBFC-MFIs are required to obtain a certificate of registration from the RBI and comply with the regulations on interest rates, lending practices, borrower protection, and reporting requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Narasimhan Committee:**

 
 
• It was appointed by the RBI in 1991 to review the financial system in India and provide recommendations for its reforms.
 
• It recommended the creation of a four-tier banking system, the establishment of asset reconstruction companies, and the liberalization of the banking sector.
 
 
 
• **Deepak Parekh Committee: **
 
 
• ​It was appointed by the RBI in 2018 to review the existing framework for the MSME sector and suggest measures to strengthen it.
 
• **It recommended the creation of a distressed asset fund, the simplification of the loan application process, and the enhancement of credit guarantee schemes.**
 
 
 
• **PK Mohanty Committee:**
 
 
• **It was appointed by the RBI in 2013 to review the regulatory framework for the NBFC sector and suggest measures to enhance its stability and development.**
 
• It recommended the creation of a new category of NBFCs for infrastructure finance, the enhancement of risk management practices, and the strengthening of the supervisory framework.

questions.question: Which force causes the trade winds of the southern hemisphere to start blowing from southwest to northeast in India after crossing the equator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coriolis force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coriolis force is an apparent force that is observed due to the rotation of the Earth.**
 
• **It deflects the path of moving objects, such as winds and ocean currents, to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.**
 
• In the southern hemisphere, the trade winds start blowing from the southeast towards the equator due to the Coriolis force.
 
• As the winds cross the equator, they are deflected to the right by the Coriolis force, causing them to blow towards the northeast in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational force**

 
 
• It is the force of attraction between two masses, such as the Earth and objects on its surface.
 
• **It is responsible for keeping objects, such as the Moon, in orbit around the Earth and for causing tides.**
 
 
 
• **Magnetic force**
 
 
• **It is the force exerted by magnets and magnetic fields.**
 
• It is responsible for the behavior of compass needles and the Earth's magnetic field, which protects the planet from harmful solar radiation.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal force**
 
 
• **It is the apparent force that is observed due to the rotation of a rotating frame of reference.**
 
• It is often used to explain the behavior of objects in circular motion, but it is not a real force as it is not caused by an interaction between two objects.

questions.question: What was the HDI value of China in 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__0.768__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The HDI is a composite index that measures the average achievements of a country in three basic dimensions of human development, namely, a long and healthy life, access to knowledge, and a decent standard of living.**
 
• HDI value of China in **2021** is **0.768**, which is considered to be a high human development score and China 's rank was **79th**.
 
• The HDI establishes "goalposts"—minimum and maximum values—for each dimension and then displays the position of each nation in respect to these values. A number between 0 and 1 is used to represent this.
 
• The higher a nation's HDI value, the higher its level of human development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The HDI is a composite summary indicator that evaluates a nation's average performance in three fundamental areas of human development: standard of living, knowledge, and health. **
 
• **The HDI is calculated by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and is used as a standard measure of human development across the world.**
 
• With the exception of 2012 and 2020–21, the HDI has been published yearly since its initial release in 1990.
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) has four categories: low human development (below 0.55), medium human development (0.55-.70), high human development (0.7-0.79), and very high human development (0.8-1.0).

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a free-enterprise economy?

options.text: Decisions are based on the forces of demand and supply.
Factor rewards are based on the productivity of factors of production.
All economic decisions are taken by the economic planners.
Economic decisions are regulated by the market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**__All economic decisions are taken by the economic planners".__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **A free-enterprise economy** is also known as a capitalist economy, where the means of production are privately owned, and economic decisions are based on the forces of demand and supply.
 
• The government does not interfere in the market unless it is necessary to ensure fair competition or protect consumers.
 
• Economic decisions are regulated by the market in a free-enterprise economy.
 
• The market mechanism determines the prices of goods and services, which, in turn, determine the production and consumption decisions of firms and consumers.
 
• Factor rewards are based on the productivity of factors of production in a free-enterprise economy. The factors of production, such as land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship, are owned by private individuals

questions.question: Which regulatory body oversees microfinance institutions in India?

options.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The RBI is the central bank of India and has the authority to regulate and supervise all financial institutions operating in the country.**
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs) are considered Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and are regulated by the RBI under the regulatory framework for NBFCs.**
 
• The RBI sets guidelines and regulations for MFIs to ensure they operate in a transparent and responsible manner, and to protect the interests of customers.
 
• The RBI also conducts regular inspections and audits of MFIs to ensure they comply with the regulations and maintain financial stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Finance:**

 
 
• Ministry of Finance plays a key role in setting policies and regulations for the financial sector in India.
 
• It specifically addresses taxation, financial regulations, capital markets, financial institutions, federal and state finances, and the Union Budget.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**
 
 
• As the name suggests, IRDAI is responsible for regulating and developing the insurance sector in India.
 
• The Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has control over the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, which is an established body.
 
 
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):**
 
 
• SEBI is the regulatory body for securities markets in India. 
 
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India was constituted as** a non-statutory body **on April 12, 1988 through a resolution of the Government of India.
 
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India was established as a **statutory body** in the year 1992 and the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992) came into force on January 30, 1992.

questions.question: Which of the following associations was formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satya Shodhak Samaj.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The association formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society is the Satya Shodhak Samaj.
 
• Satya Shodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873 with the aim to uplift the lower castes and women.
 
• **The movement challenged the** Brahminical domination** of the Indian society and advocated for social equality, education, and women's rights.**
 
• **The movement was instrumental in the** formation of the Indian National Congress and the Dalit movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theosophical Society**

 
 
• Theosophical Society is a worldwide organization that aims to promote unity and understanding among different religions and cultures.
 
• **It was founded in the United States in 1875 by Helena Petrovna Blavatsky, Henry Steel Olcott, and William Quan Judge.**
 
• The society's main objective is to study and promote theosophy, which is a set of spiritual and philosophical teachings that are believed to be universal and timeless.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj**
 
 
• ** Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 with the aim to promote Vedic knowledge and remove superstitions from Hinduism.**
 
• The movement emphasizes the authority of the Vedas and rejects idol worship, caste system, and animal sacrifices.
 
• Arya Samaj played an important role in the Indian independence movement and was a major influence on the Hindu nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Dharma Paripalana Yogam**
 
 
• Dharma Paripalana Yogam is a religious organization based in Kerala that aims to promote the teachings of Sree Narayana Guru, a social reformer and spiritual leader.
 
• **The organization is known for its work in the fields of education, healthcare, and social welfare.**
 
• Sree Narayana Guru is considered to be one of the most influential figures in the social reform movements of Kerala.

questions.question: Identify the FALSE statement.

options.text: RBI decides the bank rate for the economy
SEBI conducts open market operations to regulate money supply in the economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SEBI conducts open market operations to regulate money supply in the economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RBI decides the bank rate for the economy which is the rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.**
 
• SEBI is the Securities and Exchange Board of India which regulates the securities market and does not conduct open market operations.
 
• RBI is responsible for printing currency notes in India.
 
• **Ministry of Finance issues coins in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Open market operations are conducted by the RBI to regulate the money supply in the economy.**

 
 
• In this process, RBI buys or sells government securities in the open market to increase or decrease the money supply respectively.
 
 
 
• **SEBI is responsible for regulating the securities market in India.**
 
 
• It was established in 1988 and is headquartered in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Finance is responsible for managing the finances of the Government of India.**
 
 
• It is headed by the finance minister and is responsible for formulating and implementing the financial policies of the government.
 
 
 
• **Bank rate is the rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.**
 
 
• It is an important tool used by RBI to control the money supply in the economy.

questions.question: Which of the following words was NOT a part of the original Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**secular**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original Preamble had the following words: "We, the people of India, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Democratic Republic..."
 
• **"Democratic", "Republic", and** **"Sovereign"** were all a part of the original Preamble and continue to be integral to the Indian Constitution.
 
• **"Democratic" refers to the principle of government by the people and for the people.**
 
• **"Republic" signifies that the head of the state is elected, not hereditary.**
 
• **"Sovereign" means that India is a free and independent country that is not subject to external control.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **The Preamble of the Indian Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949.**
 
• It is an introductory statement that sets out the fundamental principles and values of the Constitution.
 
• **The Preamble originally had 22 words, but it was amended by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 to include the words "socialist" and "secular".**
 
• "Secular" was added to the Preamble in 1976 to signify that India is a country that does not have an official religion and that all religions are treated equally by the state.

questions.question: Which of the following article says that 'It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A(k)**__.

• 51A(i), states that it is the duty of every citizen to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• **51A(h), states that it is the duty of every citizen to develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true regarding the Green Revolution?

i. The term 'green revolution' was coined by Sir William Gaud.

ii. Norman Borlaug is hailed as the Father of Green Revolution.

iii. MS Randhawa is called the Father of Green Revolution in India.
questions.solution:
​​The correct answer is **__option i and ii.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sir William Gaud, a British economist, first used the term "Green Revolution" in a 1968 speech to describe the rapid increase in agricultural productivity in Asia and Latin America.
 
• **Norman Borlaug, an American plant scientist, is widely regarded as the Father of Green Revolution for his pioneering work in developing new wheat varieties that were resistant to disease and had higher yields.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** refers to a period of significant agricultural productivity growth that occurred in the 1960s and 1970s, mainly in developing countries. 
 
• **It involved the introduction of high-yielding crop varieties, modern farming techniques, and improved irrigation and fertilization practices.**
 
• **MS Randhawa** was a prominent Indian botanist and agricultural scientist, but he is not considered the Father of Green Revolution in India. 
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan**, is known as the Father of Green Revolution in India, who played a key role in introducing high-yielding varieties of rice and wheat in the country.
